clue.text: Supports British experts

parts.note: aces are people who are expert at something

explanation.surface: Someone praises the backing given by British specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Braces are straps or props that hold something up, so they are supporters.

clue.text: Card game not good for marital partner

indicators.note: not good tells us the letter for good is dropped from the card game

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A spouse is told that a game of cards is no good for a married partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman getting married is a spouse in the making, a partner in marriage.

clue.text: Current Hair performer

parts.note: AC stands for alternating current
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone appearing in the current run of the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair is the 1960s rock musical, which makes 'Current Hair performer' read as a cast member.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman who acts on stage or screen, so a performer.

clue.text: Looks at how circumscribing advertising becomes cosmetic

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it, so looks at gives eyes

indicators.note: circumscribing means drawing a line around, so the word how surrounds the letters for advertising

parts.note: taken as written
AD is short for advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone studies how an advertising campaign turns into a beauty product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks at' is a verb phrase, not a noun, and 'circumscribing' wraps the word how round the advertising abbreviation, giving HADOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye shadow is a make-up colour applied to the eyelids, so a cosmetic.

clue.text: Girl in bed before one

indicators.note: before places the bed word ahead of the word for one

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A girl is found lying in bed ahead of someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female first name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Put away by reportedly well-known school

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the school's name is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: Eton is the famous English boarding school near Windsor

explanation.surface: Something was stored by a famous school, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is England's best-known public school; said aloud ETON sounds like EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is an idiom for eating it, so it has been consumed.

clue.text: Drink at home when covering church conference

indicators.note: covering means the drink and the home word wrap around the church abbreviation

parts.note: tea is a common drink
in means at home

explanation.surface: Tea is drunk at home while a church meeting takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' means the drink-plus-home pair is split open so the church abbreviation sits between its parts; a teach-in suggests the 1960s campus protest meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal meeting with lectures and discussion on a topic, a kind of conference.

clue.text: Lady with light-coloured hair has old Ben flummoxed

indicators.note: flummoxed means confused, so the letters of has old Ben are jumbled

explanation.surface: Old Ben is bewildered by a fair-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash-blonde is a woman whose hair is a pale greyish-fair shade.

clue.text: Tennis score minus 5

annotationWithheld.why: Tennis score minus 5 (7): FIFTEEN is a tennis score, but no reading of 'minus 5' gives or confirms it, and no source found gives the parse; the clue may be misprinted

clue.text: Almost fixed a case

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: attached means fixed or fastened

explanation.surface: Someone has nearly secured a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: An attaché case is a slim briefcase; here the shortened word stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is short for an attaché case, a flat document briefcase.

clue.text: A stunt or a confused space traveller

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled person asks whether it is a stunt or an orbiting traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a person trained to travel in a spacecraft.

clue.text: Special red heels on items worn in Bavaria

indicators.note: special suggests the letters have been made into something unusual, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Bavarians wear unusual red heels with their traditional clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lederhosen are leather shorts with braces, the traditional dress of Bavarian men.

clue.text: 50% drink

definitions.meaning: fifty per cent is one of two equal parts
in a British pub you can order a ..., meaning ... a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A drink served at half strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Half is one of two equal parts, and in a pub it is half a pint of beer or cider.

clue.text: Acted like a model as asked

definitions.meaning: a model holds a position for an artist or photographer
to put a question is to ask it

explanation.surface: Someone behaved like a model when requested.
explanation.definitionFit: A model sits still for a painter, and to pose a question is to ask it.

clue.text: Complainant wants a professional assay of gold

parts.note: pro is short for professional
an assay is a test of a metal's purity
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A complaining client wants an expert to test some gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestor objects publicly to something, so is one who complains.

clue.text: Contemplative spirit in social worker

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
taken as written
the ant is a social insect, a worker in a colony

explanation.surface: A thoughtful drink of liquor in the company of a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but simply supplies its own letters; the social worker is an ant, not a council employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminant as an adjective means given to meditation or deep thought, like a cow chewing the cud.

clue.text: Zoo people go over area next to head of Great Lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means sitting on top, so the people word comes above the area letter

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Visitors to a zoo cross an area beside the top of a Great Lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes only the G from 'Great', so the Great Lakes are a false trail: the lake is simply ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for show, an early form of zoo.

clue.text: Succeed by running with bat again immediately

parts.note: to succeed someone is to follow them
on means running or operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A batsman succeeds by scoring runs, then goes out to bat once more.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a side far behind on the first innings can be made to follow on, batting again straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, to follow on is to start a second innings at once after the first.

clue.text: One in crow's-nest has to be careful

definitions.meaning: the crow's-nest is the watch platform high on a ship's mast
a warning to take care and watch for danger

explanation.surface: A sailor high on the mast has to stay alert.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor posted to watch from the masthead is a lookout, and to look out is to watch carefully.

clue.text: NHS employee runs off with drug

indicators.note: off means awry or wrong, so the word runs is rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A health worker leaves in a hurry carrying medication.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service. 'runs off' reads as fleeing, but 'off' rearranges RUNS into NURS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse cares for patients and is a typical member of hospital staff.

clue.text: A prize light wine, dry, and English

parts.note: rosé is a light pink wine
TT means teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A light, dry English wine wins an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means alcohol-free here, not a wine that is not sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize at shows and competitions.

clue.text: Emperor in period when erotic exhibitionism flourished

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler reigned at a time when sexual display was rife.
explanation.walkthrough: The remaining words describe the emperor's notoriously decadent reign and add surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman ruler of the first century AD, notorious for excess.

clue.text: Traditionally worn by business types using room before match

indicators.note: before puts the room word in front of the match word

parts.note: a lounge is a sitting room
to suit is to match, as colours suit each other

explanation.surface: Executives wear formal clothes in a lounge ahead of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge suit is a man's matching jacket and trousers, standard office wear.

clue.text: Lines on both sides of monkey jacket's folded part

indicators.note: on both sides of means the lines letters sit at each end with the monkey between them

parts.note: L stands for line, so lines is two Ls
an ape is a kind of monkey in loose use

explanation.surface: Stripes run down each side of a monkey jacket, a short naval jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: A monkey jacket is a short, close-fitting sailor's jacket, but 'monkey' here supplies APE and 'jacket's' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the turned-back front flap of a jacket below the collar.

clue.text: Creamy-white: could appear to be gold in an evergreen setting

indicators.note: in, with setting after it, shows the gold word placed within the evergreen

parts.note: ivy is an evergreen climbing plant
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A pale creamy hue could look golden against a green background.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is the pale yellowish-white colour of elephant tusk.

clue.text: Bloody-minded secret agent provides cover for French too

indicators.note: providing cover for means wrapping around, so the spy word encloses the French word

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
trop is French for too

explanation.surface: An awkward spy shields a French colleague as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and deliberately obstructive.

clue.text: Go and sort out temperature inside small caves

indicators.note: inside places the temperature letter within the rearranged letters
out means not in order, so the letters of go and sort are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and regulate the heat in some little caverns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go and sort out' reads as an instruction, but 'out' signals rearranging the first two words into GROTOS, and 'inside' slots the temperature letter in.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, natural or artificial.

clue.text: Conductor upset by series of short sharp sounds

definitions.meaning: Sir Simon ... is a famous British conductor
a clattering noise, like loose parts shaking

explanation.surface: A conductor is put off by a burst of rapid clicking noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Rattle leads orchestras, to rattle someone is to fluster them, and a rattle is a quick clatter.

clue.text: Vegetable salesman can be heard on the line

indicators.note: can be heard means a word for the salesman is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: a seller is someone who sells
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's cry is audible down the phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: SELLER said aloud gives the first part of the vegetable's name; a railway line gives RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a vegetable with long crisp pale-green stalks.
